**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate the historical Foundation lease**

When an original Foundation reservation had a missing, overlong, or already-expired lease and the lease was later corrected before Completion, this audit accepts it: no earlier predicate validates the historical lease, `stable_spec_matches` omits `leaseExpiresAt`, and this line explicitly removes `lease` from the only comparison with the current validated entry. This allows an invalid reservation to acquire completed provenance; validate the original timestamps and maximum duration against the reservation commit time before excluding later renewals from identity comparison.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recheck original claims against MOD-GOV ownership**

If the original reservation declared `**`, a non-governance path, or any shared path and later narrowed its claims before Completion, this function still accepts the reservation: checking `moduleIds == ["MOD-GOV"]` does not validate the claimed paths, while the later stable comparison deliberately ignores both path lists. Validate the original `exclusivePaths` and `sharedPaths` against the module-ownership snapshot at the reservation commit so an invalid governance reservation cannot be legitimized retroactively.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require the reservation base to equal its integration parent**

When a Foundation reservation records any stale ancestor as `baseSha`, this check accepts it because it only requires ancestry; a later activation can replace that value because `baseSha` is excluded from the stable comparison. The normal registration validator requires the recorded base to equal the actual target base, so this historical proof should likewise require `base_sha == parent`; otherwise a reservation created from an outdated baseline can later receive completed provenance.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate the complete historical Task Spec binding**

For a non-bootstrap Foundation whose original Task Spec used `coordinationMode: bootstrap`, pointed `programTaskId` or `programPlan` elsewhere, or used an unrelated `evidencePath`, this partial validation still succeeds and the fields can be corrected before Completion. `stable_spec_matches` does not inspect those fields, so checking only schema version, state, wave, role, and title does not prove that the original version-2 spec was actually registry-bound; validate the complete historical Task Spec contract at this snapshot.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require Evidence in the original reservation snapshot**

If the reservation commit adds only the Program entry, Registry entry, and Task Spec, this condition accepts it because Evidence files are merely allowed, not required; Evidence and the handoff can then be created later before Completion. That loses the auditable reservation and handoff state that must exist before implementation starts, so require the task-bound Evidence/handoff artifacts to exist in—and be introduced or updated by—the original reservation commit.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Audit every intermediate Registry state**

When a Foundation temporarily changes a stable identity or collapses `implementer` and `reviewer` to the same actor on an integrated mainline commit, then restores the valid values before Completion, this loop sees only that the task remained present and the later original-to-current comparison succeeds. Such an invalid intermediate state can authorize implementation or review before being hidden, so validate each adjacent first-parent Registry transition—or at minimum enforce stable identity and role separation at every snapshot—not just the introduction and final state.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind frozenAt validation to the reservation commit time**

For an atomic freeze whose recorded `frozenAt` was in the future when the reservation commit was created but is in the past by the time Completion is audited, this call accepts the forged chronology because `validate_recovery_transition` compares the timestamp with the current wall clock. Historical reconstruction must additionally require `frozenAt` to be no later than the reservation commit timestamp; otherwise an impossible freeze event can become valid merely by waiting.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind completion provenance to the implementation commit**

When a Foundation has any post-reservation metadata commit whose message names the task and a PR—such as its activation or Review transition—using that commit and PR as `mergeCommit`/`completionRef` passes: `validate_commit` accepts the identifiers, and these checks require only that the commit follow the reservation and appear on the audited first-parent history. The Foundation can therefore complete while permanently recording a metadata transition rather than the commit containing the repair; verify that the claimed commit contains the registered implementation changes or is bound by the reviewed implementation proof.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Archive the tested source in the candidate history**

At the reviewed commit, `6ecfcf49477341c90bc729743d05f17f2dc0dc24` is not an ancestor of the candidate (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` exits 1); both commits instead share parent `31ffefe0b4ba9a8b413a590bb46ee43ae6288dfb`. Nevertheless, this canonical inventory and the accompanying summary, handoff, commands, and raw logs identify that sibling as the tested source and even state that it is retained as the real parent. The submitted history therefore does not preserve the commit to which its verification is bound, so reviewers cannot establish that the archived results apply to the candidate and the source may disappear when its external ref is removed; archive it as an ancestor or rerun and rebind the evidence to this candidate.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject placeholder identities in the original reservation**

When the original Foundation reservation assigns placeholders such as `coordinator: TBD`, `owner: unassigned`, or `integrator: pending` and keeps them through Completion, this condition accepts the reservation because it validates only that `implementer` and `reviewer` are nonempty and unequal. The current schemas permit those placeholder strings, and the completion-time coordination checks only apply placeholder rejection to implementer/reviewer, so the task can acquire immutable completed provenance without the explicitly assigned coordinator or integrator required for the high-risk workflow; apply the same all-role placeholder validation used by `validate_foundation_registration` to this historical entry.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify the implementation-side lineage after reservation**

For a normal merge commit, `is_ancestor(reservation_commit, merge_sha)` can succeed solely through the merge commit's first parent. An implementation branch forked before the reservation, containing work performed before registration, can therefore be merged afterward and satisfy both this check and first-parent membership. Inspect the implementation-side parent or merge base so the recorded implementation actually descends from the reservation rather than merely being integrated after it.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject conflicts in the historical reservation snapshot**

When the reservation parent already contains another active task with an overlapping exclusive or shared claim, this call validates only the new Foundation's paths against module ownership; the later parent comparison merely proves the other entry was unchanged. If that other task is removed before Foundation completion, the conflicting reservation is accepted, allowing completed provenance for work that never held an exclusive path lease. Validate the target's claims against every active entry in the reconstructed reservation snapshot.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Run the current Task validator against the snapshot**

Under the repository's normal `python scripts/check-program-plan-history.py` invocation, `__file__` is relative, so this path is `scripts/check-task-file.py`; because the subprocess changes `cwd` to the historical clone, it executes the checker stored in the reservation commit rather than the current checker. After Task validation is strengthened, an older weaker checker can therefore approve a historical spec that the completion gate is meant to reject, while these unit tests miss the discrepancy because they invoke the history script through an absolute path. Resolve the validator path to an absolute current-worktree path before launching it.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recheck dependencies at the reservation snapshot**

If a Foundation lists a dependency that is still incomplete when its reservation is integrated, but that dependency completes before this Foundation's completion, this call only proves that the `dependsOn` text matched the Registry and never checks the dependency's status in the reconstructed Program snapshot. The invalid reservation therefore gains completed provenance even though implementation was allowed to start before its prerequisite contract entered the baseline; validate every original dependency against `plan` at the reservation commit.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate implementation against the pre-change scope**

When an implementation commit broadens its own `exclusivePaths` in `active-work.yaml` and modifies a newly claimed file in the same commit, loading the Registry from `commit` makes the broadened post-change claims authorize that diff; `active-work.yaml` itself is then excluded from `implementation_paths`, and the claims can be restored before Completion because they are treated as mutable. This permits implementation outside the previously registered lease, so validate against the first-parent entry or require a separate metadata-only scope amendment before the implementation commit.

When the lease is expired or otherwise invalid at the claimed implementation commit but is renewed before Completion, this audit accepts the history because only the original lease is validated and the snapshot loop explicitly excludes `lease` from comparison without validating it. Fresh evidence in this revision is that the new loop classifies `lease` as mutable while checking only stable identity and role separation. Validate each snapshot's lease against that commit's timestamp so work performed without a valid lease cannot acquire completed provenance.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate the complete rebased implementation range**

For a task using the supported `rebase` integration strategy, the recorded `mergeCommit` can be the last of several consecutive rebased commits, but this checks only that final commit against its immediate parent. An earlier rebased commit can therefore change an unclaimed path while the final commit changes one valid claimed file, causing Completion to accept the unauthorized change; an evidence-only final commit can also reject an otherwise valid implementation. Validate every commit in the integrated implementation range, or diff the complete range from its pre-integration base to the recorded tip.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recognize registered policy-only repairs as implementation**

When a governance Foundation's legitimate implementation consists solely of changes to Program/Registry policy, filtering out the entire `PLAN` and `ACTIVE` documents leaves `implementation_paths` empty and rejects the recorded merge as lifecycle-only. Repository policy explicitly contemplates pure Program/Registry policy repairs while requiring them to remain bound to a stable registered task, so compare those documents structurally and exclude only the task's lifecycle fields rather than excluding both files wholesale.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject unrelated reservations in an already-frozen Program**

When the parent and reservation snapshots are already frozen for recovery task A, a newly added Foundation B skips this branch because it handles only an `active`→`frozen` transition owned by B; removing B then makes the remaining Program and Registry compare equal, so B's reservation is accepted and can later receive completed provenance. Require the original reservation either to occur while the Program is active or to be the atomic freeze owned by that same task, since only the declared, already-registered recovery Foundation may proceed during a freeze.

When the reservation parent already has `maxActiveTasks` active entries or one high-risk task, adding this high-risk Foundation exceeds the Registry limits, but the reconstructed snapshot only checks conflicts and dependencies. If another task leaves before Completion, the invalid reservation is accepted and gains completed provenance; count the parent’s active/high-risk entries against `previous_active.policy` before accepting the introduction.

When another active task acquires an overlapping exclusive or shared claim after this Foundation’s valid reservation but before its claimed implementation commit, this validation accepts the implementation because it checks only ownership and whether changed files match this task’s claims. Removing the other task before Completion then hides that the repair ran without an exclusive lease, so compare the implementation snapshot’s claims with every other active Registry entry here.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Schema-validate the reconstructed Registry**

When the original Active Work entry contains a schema-invalid value that persists until Completion—such as an unknown property or a string-valued `issue`—this check accepts it because it verifies only that `tasks` is a list and later compares the same malformed entry with the prior Completion entry. The current Registry becomes schema-valid as soon as Completion removes that entry, so the invalid reservation can acquire completed provenance; validate the reconstructed `active-work.yaml` against its applicable schema before using it.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify all lifecycle documents at the implementation commit**

When the claimed commit has an `in_progress` Registry entry but its Task Spec or Foundation Program record is still `reserved` (or otherwise disagrees), this condition accepts the implementation because it inspects only the Registry status. A later Review commit can synchronize those documents before Completion, permanently hiding that implementation occurred before the required lifecycle transition; load the claimed commit’s Task Spec and Program entry and require their status and task binding to match the active Registry snapshot.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject reviewer-role commits as implementation**

When a commit changes a claimed implementation file while the historical entry is in `review` with `agentRole: reviewer`, this condition accepts it because `review` is included in `IMPLEMENTATION_STATES` and the role is never checked. Completion can then bind the reviewer’s unreviewed code change as the implementation merge, defeating the required separation; reject direct implementation changes made in the reviewer role unless the commit is proven to be an integration of an already independently reviewed implementation.

When OPS-004 is reserved alongside another high-risk task, this branch records `capacityResult: "FAIL"` but returns without adding an error, allowing that over-capacity reservation and its later implementation nodes to acquire completed provenance. Fresh evidence in this revision is the explicit task/SHA-specific exemption for exactly two high-risk tasks; an Owner evidence file cannot override the rule that governance recovery remains subject to concurrency limits, so this case must remain a validation failure.

When work was committed before reservation and that old branch later merges the reservation commit before being integrated, the resulting side tip satisfies `is_ancestor(reservation_commit, side)` even though the actual implementation commit predates registration. **<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Ignore base-reachable changes in side-merge diffs**

When an implementation branch merges the latest main before integration and main contains unrelated changes outside this task’s claims, `base..commit` correctly excludes those main commits, but this per-node diff compares the synchronization merge only with its first parent. The main-side files therefore reappear in `node_implementation` and are rejected as out of scope even though they are already present in the integration base. Because tasks must synchronize latest main before Review, valid merge-strategy Foundations can be blocked; exclude changes reachable from `base` when inspecting merge nodes or evaluate their parent deltas appropriately.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Revalidate path claims at every Registry snapshot**

When a metadata-only amendment temporarily changes `exclusivePaths` to overlap another active task and that task leaves before implementation, Completion accepts the history: both path lists are treated as mutable, while the snapshot loop validates only schema, lease, stable fields, and role separation. The later working-node check then sees no conflict, hiding a Registry state that never held a valid exclusive lease. Fresh evidence in this revision is that the path lists remain excluded here without ownership or conflict validation; revalidate claims against ownership and every contemporaneous active entry at each snapshot.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Limit integrator code to proven integration commits**

When a single-parent code commit sets `agentRole: integrator`, this condition accepts it exactly like an implementer commit. Fresh evidence in this revision is the unconditional integrator allowance without checking that the node actually integrates independently implemented and reviewed history; an integrator can therefore add new, unreviewed repair code during the Review→Integration transition and bind that commit as the implementation. **<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject cross-task lifecycle edits in implementation nodes**

When a claimed implementation commit also removes or rewrites another task’s Registry entry, `ACTIVE` is discarded from `node_implementation`, and the remaining checks inspect only this Foundation’s entry plus aggregate schema and capacity. The foreign entry can therefore have its assigned reviewer, lease, status, or claims changed and then be restored before Completion without invalidating the recorded implementation history. **<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Pin historical capacity checks to the approved policy**

When a metadata-only commit after reservation temporarily raises `active-work.policy.maxHighRiskTasks` from 1 to 2, later work nodes pass capacity validation because this call trusts that mutable historical policy; the Registry schema itself permits values up to 3. Restoring the policy before Completion hides the change because the snapshot loop never compares policy values. Fresh evidence here is that working-node capacity is evaluated against the mutable Registry limit rather than the approved Program limit, allowing two high-risk tasks to run despite the fixed concurrency rule; reject historical policy changes or validate against the canonical policy.

When a side branch merges a main commit that is an ancestor of `base` but not the latest one, resolving an unclaimed file to that stale parent's blob causes this function to discard the path merely because it matches an `incoming` parent. A later merge of the actual base can similarly discard the restoration, while the net `base..commit` diff contains neither change, so both transient out-of-scope commits pass the history audit. Only exclude an imported entry when it also matches the audited base state, or otherwise prove the synchronization parent is the exact approved base.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate each historical Program snapshot before mapping it**

When an implementation node temporarily adds a schema-invalid or duplicate own `foundationTasks` record and restores it before Completion, `mapping()` collapses duplicate task IDs and this check validates only the selected record's status and title; the foreign-metadata comparison also removes every record for this task. The audit can therefore accept work performed while the authoritative Program identity or provenance was ambiguous or schema-invalid. Validate each reconstructed Program document, including task-ID uniqueness, before deriving the Foundation record.
